statements.text: Is there any way that we could proactively protect against AI-generated cyber attacks?
statements.context: Rep. Tim Burchett poses a question during a House hearing titled "Advances in AI: Are We Ready for a Tech Revolution?"

statements.text: But the development of AI, how will that impact our international relations specifically with China? I fear what they will do if they get control of it, as you have stated there.
statements.context: House Oversight subcommittee hearing on AI advances where Rep. Burchett questions a witness about geopolitical implications of AI development.

statements.text: This, for lack of a better term, has scared the hell out of me. [...] what I have heard today is unlike anything I have ever heard, particularly in terms of our national security. [...] Dr. Ma˛dry, you, in your testimony, talked about the overarching points. And the fourth one you talked about was that we pay atten- tion, critical attention, to the artificial intelligence supply chain, that it will structure the distribution of power in a new AI world. Could you take just a moment to explain that?
statements.context: House Oversight Subcommittee hearing on AI advances, where Rep. Burchett reacts to expert testimony and questions Dr. Madry on the AI supply chain.

statements.text: Do you all agree that these AI-generated images of children, real or not, should be illegal?
statements.context: Rep. Tim Burchett posed a question during a House hearing on advances in deepfake technology.

statements.text: what national security concerns exist regarding AI that justifies using the Defense Production Act?
statements.context: Asked during a House hearing titled 'White House Overreach on AI'.

statements.text: Do you think using the Defense Production Act to regulate artificial intelligence is a bit of an overreach, and would Congress be better suited to regulate artificial intelligence?
statements.context: Rep. Tim Burchett questioning a witness during a House Oversight Subcommittee hearing on executive-branch AI regulation.

statements.text: Yes, my biggest fear with this, again, is we do not understand it. [...] But here again, we are going to start reg- ulating something we do not understand because we are govern- ment and we are supposed to, and then, again, it is just like cryptocurrency and everything else, dadgummit. We will end up hurting it, you know, so that is my concern.
statements.context: House subcommittee hearing titled "White House Overreach on AI," where Rep. Tim Burchett questions a witness and then yields back his time.

statements.text: we have heard a lot about this already from people testi- fying and even from Members here, that it is not just about having AI, it is about having to deploy AI in a responsible way and in a manner in which we are not letting AI make mistakes. I will give you an example. In Michigan about, let us say, 10 years ago now, they deployed AI to try to find fraud, and they ended up finding a lot of fraud where there was not any fraud.
statements.context: House hearing on the Federal Government in the Age of Artificial Intelligence, during the questioning portion led by Rep. Subramanyam.

statements.text: The majority of East Tennesseans and, frankly, Tennesseans and Americans, are worried about their privacy being violated by government artificial intelligence programs. What do you think Congress can do to protect our privacy? And my biggest fear in all this is Congress.
statements.context: Verbatim remarks during a House Oversight Committee hearing titled "The Federal Government in the Age of Artificial Intelligence."

statements.text: The majority of East Ten- nesseans and, frankly, Tennesseans and Americans, are worried about their privacy being violated by government artificial intel- ligence programs. What do you think Congress can do to protect our privacy? [...] some of these cats up here still have eight-track tape players in their 1972 AMC Gremlins, and they are going to try to regulate AI. They cannot hardly spell ‘‘AI’’ and now we are going to regulate it, so.
statements.context: House committee hearing titled "The Federal Government in the Age of Artificial Intelligence," featuring witness testimony on AI policy.
